en.title: Raised by Wolves Producer Confirms Merger Killed Season 3
en.summary: The acclaimed sci-fi series 'Raised by Wolves' was axed by HBO Max, and a key producer has now pinpointed the exact cause. Fans are still reeling from the abrupt end to Mother and Father's journey.
en.body:
The dream of a third season for Aaron Guzikowski's ambitious sci-fi drama **Raised by Wolves** was extinguished not by dwindling viewership or creative fatigue, but by corporate restructuring. The shocking cancellation in June 2022 left fans and cast members reeling, but the precise reason has now been confirmed by a key figure behind the scenes.

David W. Zucker, Chief Creative Officer at **Ridley Scott**’s Scott Free Productions, has officially stated that the massive WarnerMedia and Discovery Inc. merger was the death knell for the series. The integration of these two media giants led to significant shifts in programming strategy, and unfortunately, **Raised by Wolves** found itself on the chopping block. Zucker explained that the arrival of new CEO **David Zaslav** precipitated the decision to shelve the show, directly impacting the production of its planned third season.

> "I personally wish that we would be able to bring Raised by Wolves back," Zucker told ScreenRant, expressing a sentiment surely shared by the show's dedicated fanbase. He also noted the unpredictable nature of the industry, referencing how he "never thought we would make an Alien or Blade Runner series" before Scott Free Productions went on to develop **Alien: Earth** and the upcoming **Blade Runner 2099** miniseries. This suggests that while **Raised by Wolves** may be gone, the hope for its potential revival, however slim, hasn't been entirely abandoned by its creators.

## The Cost of Corporate Synergy

The cancellation of **Raised by Wolves** serves as a stark reminder of how external business decisions can abruptly derail compelling storytelling. The series, which premiered on HBO Max in September 2020 and was renewed for a second season shortly after, presented a unique vision of humanity's future. It followed two androids, Mother and Father, tasked with raising human children on a distant planet after Earth was destroyed by a war between atheists and a religious faction known as the Mithraic. The show's intricate mythology, stunning visuals, and complex character arcs garnered a passionate following, making its premature end all the more frustrating for its audience.

## A Glimmer of Hope?

Fans who have been desperately hoping for a Season 3 will find little solace in the confirmation of the merger's impact, but Zucker’s continued advocacy for the show offers a sliver of optimism. While HBO Max moved on, the producer's desire to see the series continue suggests that Scott Free Productions might explore other avenues for its resurrection. The sci-fi landscape is constantly evolving, with platforms eager to acquire unique and engaging content, and the enduring appeal of **Raised by Wolves** could still find a new home.

## What's Next

Details regarding any potential revival efforts for **Raised by Wolves** have not yet been announced. In the meantime, fans can revisit the first two seasons, which are currently available on Max, or were formerly available on, HBO Max. Scott Free Productions continues to develop new projects, including **Alien: Earth** and **Blade Runner 2099**.

content_raw: Fans of Aaron Guzikowski’s Raised by Wolves were gutted to hear that there would be no season 3 of the acclaimed sci-fi series back in June 2022. At the time, Abubakar Salim, who led the cast as Father alongside Amanda Collin as Mother, suggested that the huge WarnerMedia and Discovery Inc. merger was responsible for Raised by Wolves ’ sudden cancelation, which has now been confirmed by David W. Zucker, CCO at Ridley Scott ’s Scott Free Productions. Zucker told ScreenRant that the merger was indeed to blame for Raised by Wolves ’ fate, noting that new CEO “David Zaslav [came] in” and that led to “our third season [getting] set aside” by HBO Max, adding, “I personally wish that we would be able to bring Raised by Wolves back,” and noting that he “never thought we would make an Alien or Blade Runner series” so keeps “hoping that [show] might have another day.” The Raised by Wolves producer was, of course, referring to two of Scott Free Productions’ newer offerings, Alien: Earth , currently in production on a second season , and Blade Runner 2099 , an upcoming miniseries set to debut on Prime Video in 2027. Still, you can sense that Raised by Wolves has certainly not been forgotten by those behind the scenes, even with some shiny new toys to play with. Raised by Wolves imagined a future version of Earth that had been destroyed in a war between atheists and a religious group called the Mithraic. In the aftermath, two androids (Collin’s Mother and Salim’s Father) were sent to a distant planet along with human embryos in an effort to start a society of peaceful atheists. However, this plan was disrupted when Mithraic colonists also arrived and reignited the old feud between the two groups. Not only that, their new planet was full of secrets that challenged both religious and scientific explanations, and many of the show’s mysteries were left unresolved after the show’s abrupt cancellation. After the WBD merger, the series was removed from HBO Max, and it is still searching for a streaming home.
